documents.title: Guiding Principles for Everyone
documents.summary: Campus-wide guiding principles grouped as integrity, transparency, access and AI literacy. They stress data protection, verifying output, disclosure, equitable access and training for all users.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no ban or tiers; it lists duties that assume AI use under conditions: 'Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated', 'Verify AI output before accepting it as fact' and 'Refrain from inputting personal or confidential information into AI tools'. It leaves course rules to other pages, but its own stance is conditional permission.

units.why: Directive 'Refrain from inputting personal or confidential information' protects data, so P50 with must-not.
units.anchor: Refrain from inputting personal or confidential information into AI tools.

units.why: 'Ensure ... in accordance with risk classification and security and FERPA' ties AI use to existing rules, so P77 (comply with law and policy).
units.anchor: Ensure all AI tools are used in accordance with risk classification and security

units.why: 'Ensure all data is deidentified' is a data-protection duty, so P50.
units.anchor: Ensure all data is deidentified when using in an AI tool.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. The sentence is a data-protection duty for all campus users in a general principles list, not tied to an assignment. Final phase general (B).

units.why: 'human oversight ... to verify accuracy' asks users to check AI output, so P31 rather than P73 (no decision about a person).
units.anchor: Provide human oversight for AI-generated content to verify accuracy and minimize bias.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. Guidance addressed to all campus users (staff, faculty, students), not tied to a stage of a course, so phase is general. Final phase general (B).

units.why: 'Protect intellectual property rights; avoid ... inputting journal articles or other copyrighted materials in non-enterprise tools' is a copyright rule (P52).
units.anchor: avoid intentionally inputting journal articles or other copyrighted materials in non-enterprise tools
units.fit_note: Also limits inputs to non-enterprise tools, which P52 (licensing of inputs and outputs) only partly captures.
units.resolution_why: A coded P49 (should-not), B coded P52 (must, merged with the preceding clause). The source reads 'Protect intellectual property rights; avoid intentionally inputting journal articles or other copyrighted materials in non-enterprise tools.' P49 is about uploading course materials, and journal articles are not course materials, so the copyright framing (P52) fits better. 'avoid' is soft, so modality is should-not (A), not must. The anchor is the 'avoid' clause and states the rule itself, so policy is null. Phase general as for the other items in this list.

units.why: 'Verify AI output before accepting it as fact' is the verify-output rule, P31.
units.anchor: Verify AI output before accepting it as fact.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. Guidance addressed to all campus users (staff, faculty, students), not tied to a stage of a course, so phase is general. Final phase general (B).

units.why: 'generate content that encourages fair representation' addresses bias in output, so P53 with should.
units.anchor: actively work to generate content that encourages fair representation
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. Guidance addressed to all campus users (staff, faculty, students), not tied to a stage of a course, so phase is general. Final phase general (B).

units.why: This sentence states a fact about bias ('may unintentionally perpetuate existing biases'), an informs-level P53.
units.anchor: may unintentionally perpetuate existing biases and inequalities

units.why: Says users 'must be aware of and actively address' limitations and biases, a bias concern (P53); P31 is about checking output specifically.
units.anchor: inherent limitations and potential biases that users must be aware of and actively address
units.fit_note: Also tells users to 'actively address' the limitations and biases, which P53 (naming bias and harms) does not capture; P31 (verify output) covers the checking duty but not the bias statement.
units.resolution_why: A coded P31, B coded P53. The sentence says 'AI tools come with inherent limitations and potential biases that users must be aware of and actively address'. It names limitations and bias as facts users must know, which is P53; P31 is the narrower duty to check output and is already coded on the neighbouring 'Verify AI output' unit. Final P53 with fit_note; the anchor states the rule, so policy is null.

units.why: 'Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance' asks users to keep their own thinking central, so P32 with should (no 'must').
units.anchor: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase (A during-work, B over-time). 'over-time' is for review of policy or evidence; this is a user's own habit while using AI, so during-work (A). B's fit_note about periodic self-evaluation is kept.
units.fit_note: Frames it as periodic self-evaluation, not only a rule about being the primary problem-solver.

units.why: 'Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated' is a disclosure duty (P24); P25 fits only partly because it asks for tool and manner of use but not the prompt or output.
units.anchor: Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, including what tool was used and how AI was
units.policy: Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, including what tool was used and how AI was used.
units.fit_note: Asks for tool and manner of use, not the exact prompt or output. | Requires the tool and manner of use, not prompts or outputs as in P25.
units.resolution_why: A coded P25 with unit_stance require, B coded P24 neutral. The source says 'Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, including what tool was used and how AI was used'. The core rule is disclosure (P24); P25 needs the prompt or output, which are not asked for. Disclosure does not require AI use, so unit_stance is neutral. Both coders' fit_notes are kept.

units.why: 'Provide disclaimers up-front when AI will assist in decision-making' is a duty to tell people AI is involved, P103.
units.anchor: Provide disclaimers up-front when AI will assist in decision-making.

units.why: 'disclaimers for AI chat assistants' tell users they deal with AI and its limits, so P103.
units.anchor: Provide disclaimers for AI chat assistants, informing users of the potential for incorrect information
units.fit_note: Also adds a prompt to double-check outputs, which is verification advice.

units.why: 'Use AI tools to create inclusive and accessible materials' treats AI as an accessibility aid, P97.
units.anchor: Use AI tools to create inclusive and accessible materials, such as multilingual content or screen-reader
units.policy: Use AI tools to create inclusive and accessible materials, such as multilingual content or screen-reader friendly documents.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. Guidance addressed to all campus users (staff, faculty, students), not tied to a stage of a course, so phase is general. Final phase general (B).

units.why: 'equitable access ... free or university provided software' is the equity rule P51.
units.anchor: Advocate for equitable access to AI tools across the university, including free or university provided
units.policy: Advocate for equitable access to AI tools across the university, including free or university provided software for those without personal resources.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on unit_stance (A neutral, B encourage). 'Advocate for equitable access to AI tools ... including free or university provided software' pushes for wider AI access, so encourage (B).

units.why: 'participate in AI Pilots on campus to explore AI use' encourages joining pilots; no type fits.
units.anchor: Encourage faculty, staff, and students to participate in AI Pilots on campus to explore AI
units.policy: Encourage faculty, staff, and students to participate in AI Pilots on campus to explore AI use.
units.uncovered_note: Campus-wide encouragement to join AI pilot programs, which no type covers (not training, not tool provision). | Encourages participation in campus AI pilots to explore AI use.

units.why: 'should complete the Generative AI Cybersecurity Awareness Bridge Training' is training for all users, P70.
units.anchor: should complete the Generative AI Cybersecurity Awareness Bridge Training

units.why: 'Attend campus training sessions' is AI-literacy training, P70.
units.anchor: Attend campus training sessions to understand how to critically assess AI-generated output.

units.why: 'Familiarize yourself with the ethical implications' asks users to keep informed, P102.
units.anchor: Familiarize yourself with the ethical implications of using AI in your role and apply best
units.policy: Familiarize yourself with the ethical implications of using AI in your role and apply best practices.
units.fit_note: Focuses on ethics and best practices rather than on developments or current guidance.

units.why: 'rapid evolution of the AI tools ... continuous learning' is a stay-informed rule, P102.
units.anchor: Recognize the rapid evolution of the AI tools and embrace a mindset of continuous learning.

units.why: 'a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning' says AI must not replace the user's own work, P32.
units.anchor: Recognize the use of AI as a tool, not a solution or replacement for work
units.policy: Recognize the use of AI as a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning.

units.why: 'Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI' asks the whole community to discuss AI; P66 is specifically instructors explaining rules to students, so I use UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI
units.policy: Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI in addition to the ethics of using AI at the university.
units.uncovered_note: Asks that discussions of the benefits, limitations and ethics of AI be prioritized at the university.
units.resolution_why: Source says 'Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI in addition to the ethics of using AI'. P66 is about instructors explaining or discussing the course's AI rules with students; this is a call for general community discussion of AI benefits, limits and ethics, so it does not say what P66 says. The same sentence recurs in all three guiding-principles pages, so it is kept UNCOVERED and logged as a candidate new type. Unit stance is neutral because it asks for discussion, not for or against AI use.

documents.title: Faculty Guiding Principles
documents.summary: Faculty principles require a syllabus statement and assignment-level AI statements, restrict AI grading to cases with student approval, and treat AI detectors as a starting point only. They also ask for disclosure of AI-made materials, equity of tools and AI-literacy teaching.
documents.stance_why: The page tells instructors to 'Create a syllabus statement for each course' with their own 'stance on AI' and to 'Include AI use statements in assignments', so it sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors and assignments.

units.why: The first clause 'should be clearly stated in the syllabus' makes instructors tell students about their AI grading/feedback, P47.
units.anchor: should be clearly stated in the syllabus
units.policy: Use of AI to grade or give feedback on assignments should be clearly stated in the syllabus.
units.resolution_why: A coded the syllabus-disclosure clause as P47 and split off the approval clause; B coded one merged P101 unit. The sentence is 'should be clearly stated in the syllabus and have explicit approval from students'; these are two rules (disclosure, consent), so they are two units. The first is disclosure of instructor AI use to students (P47). A's policy was null but the anchor lacks its subject, so a policy is written.

units.why: The second clause 'explicit approval from students' sets a consent condition on AI grading/feedback, so P101 (conditions) not P46 (no ban on AI grading).
units.anchor: have explicit approval from students
units.policy: Use of AI to grade or give feedback on assignments should have explicit approval from students.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B merged it into its single P101 unit). Checked against the source: 'Use of AI to grade or give feedback on assignments should be clearly stated in the syllabus and have explicit approval from students.' The approval clause is a separate rule (consent as a condition on AI grading, P101), so the unit is kept. A's policy was null but the anchor lacks its subject, so a policy is written.

units.why: 'offer a human-alternative ... for those who do not consent' is a condition on AI grading, P101.
units.anchor: Instructors should offer a human-alternative (e.g., teacher, TA) for those who do not consent.
units.fit_note: Also functions as an equity alternative for students who decline. | Also an opt-out alternative for students, as in P51.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase (A during-work, B course-start). The human alternative is offered when AI grading is applied, like the neighbouring consent and FERPA units, so during-work (A). Both fit_notes are kept.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to grade assignments ... without prior approval from students' conditions AI grading on consent, P101.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to grade assignments or input student work/information without prior approval from
units.policy: Do not use AI to grade assignments or input student work/information without prior approval from students

units.anchor: Ensure all data is deidentified when using in an AI tool.

'Prioritize using vetted UNO enterprise tools when using AI in your work' is a tool-choice duty for faculty's work generally, not a course stage, so phase general (B). It does not say anything for or against AI use, so unit_stance neutral (A).

units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Source: 'Due to the unreliability and bias of AI detection tools, ...' is the stated reason for the detection-tool evidence rule that follows; it is a real statement (that detectors are unreliable), so kept as an informs unit.

units.why: 'a starting point for discussion, not as conclusive evidence' limits detector output to supporting evidence, P69 (broadened) rather than P39 which is the reliability claim.
units.anchor: should be a starting point for discussion, not as conclusive evidence
units.fit_note: Detector may still be used to start a conversation; P39 says detectors are not relied on.

units.why: 'should not rely solely on one accountability measurement' is an evidence standard for misuse findings, P69.
units.anchor: should not rely solely on one accountability measurement

units.anchor: Ensure AI integration in your class promotes ethical and responsible use of AI.

units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors (supply guidelines), not to students (disclose). | Addressed to instructors (supply guidelines) rather than students (must disclose).
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on modality (A must, B should). 'Provide students with citation or attribution guidelines for AI use' is an unhedged imperative in a list of duties, so must (A).

units.why: 'fostering discussions about fairness and inclusion' means discussing AI in class with students (P66).
units.anchor: Address potential AI biases by fostering discussions about fairness and inclusion
units.fit_note: Frames bias as something to discuss in class. | Topic is bias and fairness rather than the course's AI rules.
units.resolution_why: A coded P53, B coded P66. The sentence 'Address potential AI biases by fostering discussions about fairness and inclusion' tells instructors to discuss AI bias with students; the operative act is fostering discussion, which P66 covers (discussing AI in class). P53 is for naming bias or harms, which this does not do itself. Final P66 with fit_note.

units.why: 'cross check results ... to ensure accuracy and reliability' is P31, addressed to faculty.
units.anchor: Always think critically about AI output; cross check results with web searches
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. Checking AI output is done while using AI (student page units for the same sentence are during-work), so during-work (A).

units.why: 'analyze AI output for bias and stereotypes' is a check of AI output, P31.

units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase. Analyzing AI output happens while using AI, so during-work (A).

units.why: 'prevent an overreliance on the tool' keeps the person as primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on phase (A general, B over-time). 'over-time' is for review of policy or evidence; this is an ongoing check by the user while using AI, so during-work.
units.fit_note: Periodic self-evaluation duty.

units.anchor: Create a syllabus statement for each course that includes:
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on unit_stance (A neutral, B require). 'Create a syllabus statement for each course' requires a statement, not AI use, so unit_stance is neutral (A).

units.anchor: Support and encourage continuous learning; attend workshops, webinars, etc.
units.resolution_why: Coders differ only on unit_stance (A neutral, B encourage). The unit is about faculty learning and workshops, not about AI use itself, so neutral (A).

notes: Only university-layer documents exist (no school or computing documents found; course layer deferred). Reconciled from two coders. Coder A notes: Only university-layer documents exist (no school or computing documents found). The integrity policy is long and mostly generic; I coded only the AI clauses plus a few core procedure steps (suspicion, student response, reporting, sanction ceiling) with fit notes, because they govern AI misuse once AI is listed as cheating. Faculty page: one sentence on AI grading is split into a syllabus-disclosure unit and an approval unit (same sentence, two anchors). Coder B notes: General integrity procedures (reporting, mediation, appeal, repeat offenses) in the Academic Integrity Policy are not AI-specific and were not coded as units; they apply to AI misuse by implication. Prioritize-discussions and AI-pilot lines recur across the guiding-principles pages and were coded UNCOVERED; candidate new types: community discussion of AI benefits/limits; participation in campus AI pilots; no use of AI explanation to contest a grade. Reconciler: the three guiding-principles pages repeat the sentence 'Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI'; it is UNCOVERED on all three and proposed as a new type with the AI-pilots and grade-contest items. General integrity procedure steps found only by coder A are kept with a fit_note because the integrity policy lists unauthorized AI use as cheating. The 'neutral' unit_stance is used for disclosure and procedure duties that do not take a position on AI use.
